meters.label: Duplicate posts on the page just shown

frames.narration: Offset pagination. The client loads page 1 of a feed, 5 posts per page, newest first.
While the client reads, a new post (21) is published at the top. Everything shifts down by one.
The client asks for page 2. The database skips the first 5 rows, but those are now 21 to 17, so page 2 starts at 16, the post the client already saw.
Offset also has to walk past every skipped row. Page 10,000 means skipping 50,000 rows first, so it gets slower the deeper you go.
Cursor pagination. The response to page 1 includes a cursor meaning 'last seen: post 16'.
The next request says 'posts older than 16'. New post 21 at the top does not matter, because the query starts from 16.
The page is exactly posts 15 to 11, with no duplicate, and it costs the same however deep the client has gone.
